text:
tara: heads-up — saw a reproducible slow memory creep on streaming chat sessions around 30–60m. looks like KV pages never drop once session gets past ~8k tokens. attaching a tiny ascii sparkline from our profiler

oliver: can you paste repro steps + sample prompt?

tara: repro: start toolloop with 4 agents, enable streaming, feed chained tool calls (~2-4 tokens per call) until ~9k tokens. run for ~45m. command used: `./run_local --mode=stream --agents=4 --max-steps=5000`

priya: interesting — I saw something similar but suspected "holdcount staircase" where refs increment but eviction window doesn't trigger because sequential page reuse keeps bumping residency. did you capture kv stats?

tara: yes. snippet from /proc/kv_stats during run:
```
kv_resident_pages: 19834
kv_free_pages: 1204
kv_hold_count_hist: 0:120 1:600 2:1200 3:980 4:540 5+:16800
eviction_cycles: 12
last_evict_time_s: 3590
```

sam: that hold_count histogram screams pinned ranges. 5+ is huge. could be our pager failing to coalesce duplicates or a reuse pattern that prevents page aging. any kernel selection changes?

tara: runtime recently picked `kernels_v3` for better matmul perf; we also toggled batching heuristic to prefer smaller batches for latency. change rolled 3 days ago.

oliver: hm. kernel change could alter memory access patterns (cache lines, prefetch stride) leading to less page eviction pressure. but holdcount hints at references not being released. can you run with `--kv-debug=refs` and a short trace?

priya: also try forcing a compaction sweep after every 500 steps: `echo 1 > /sys/runtime/kv_compact_trigger` and see if memory drops. If it does, it's fragmentation not leak.

tara: ran `--kv-debug=refs` for 20m and dumped trace, attaching condensed lines:
```
[00:12:04] page 0x7f8a4 ref++ (toolloop) session=abcd
[00:12:04] page 0x7f8a4 ref++ (stream) session=abcd
[00:12:04] page 0x7f8a4 ref-- (toolloop)
[00:12:04] page 0x7f8a4 ref stays 1 (stream)
...
[00:47:59] page 0x7f8a4 ref++ reused by new token prefix, never reaches 0
```

sam: looks like short-lived ref++/ref-- sequences but another path re-refs before it can hit 0. classic reuse race. Could be batching heuristic holding kv handles across micro-batches.

priya: does the session-level KV cache retain handles when we fall back from batched to single-request mode? maybe fallback path forgot to call `release_kv_handle()` on failures.

tara: searching code — found a path in `stream_batcher.go` where on partial-send error we `log.Error` and return without calling `defer release`. grabbing patch now.

oliver: good find. even if fix removes some pins, we should add telemetry: meter holdcount>3 spikes and emit a perf trace event so we can correlate with kernel selection and batching mode.

sam: agreed. PR suggestion: 1) add `defer` to release in error path, 2) add `kv_handle_hysteresis` metric, 3) small unit test to simulate partial-send and ensure release happens.

tara: created draft PR #4821 with the `defer` fix and local test. initial run looks promising: resident pages drop from ~19.8k to ~12.3k after compaction. still seeing slow upward drift but much reduced.

priya: residual drift could be fragmentation. try enabling per-session slot coalescing in the runtime config: `kv.coalesce_on_idle=true` and run longer. also toggle kernel to `kernels_v2` to compare access pattern effects.

tara: ran A/B for 2 hours: v2 + coalesce = stable at ~11.8k resident pages; v3 without coalesce = slow creep to ~13.5k. swapping kernels flips trend.

oliver: conclusion: two contributors — a bug in error path causing pinned handles (fixable) and an access-pattern dependent fragmentation effect arising from kernels_v3 interacting with our coalescer.

sam: next steps: ship PR for release, add metric + alert if holdcount_5plus > 1000 for 5m, and add an e2e perf test that runs a 1h streaming toolloop and asserts resident pages < 12k. Also file infra ticket to test kernel variants under long-stream load.

ci-bot: build passed for PR #4821 (linux-amd64), tests=74/74, perf-smoke queued. :white_check_mark:

tara: thanks all — I'll push the PR and schedule a kernel-variant perf run on staging tomorrow. I'll drop results here. :thumbsup:
